newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil shares extend bull run.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil shares extend bull run.

text.p: Prices of Nigerian oil company shares continued to soar on Tuesday as investors appetite for them remained healthy, traders said.
But the all-share index closed barely changed at 6654.48 from 6654.49 on Monday.

"Many investors are buying to reap gains of the expected privatisation of oil businesses in the coming year," one trader said, adding "They believe the business will be better managed and more profitable when government leaves the scene as it is promising to do."
Total led Tuesday's gainers with 80 kobo to 51.50 naira. Unipetrol also rose 49 kobo to 48.00 naira while National Oil jumped to 39.40 naira, up 40 kobo.
Nigerian Breweries closed stronger on the back of renewed interest. It touched 12.00 naira after adding 45 kobo.
Nestle Foods went 60 kobo up to 40.80 naira because of its recent strong showings, traders said.
FSB International Bank picked 10 kobo to five naira after announcing an improved half-year profit.
Shares of West African Portland Cement were unchanged after it reported a sharp fall in profit for the first half of 1996.
Pfizer Products lost 30 kobo to 7.20 naira because investors sold large volumes of the stock. There was a single deal for 2.1 million shares at the new price.

Conglomerates were under pressure again on Tuesday. John Holt fell 18 kobo to 10.00 naira while Lever Brothers shed five at 25.10 naira. There was no respite for CFAO, the Franco-Nigerian trading company, which slumped to 3.85 naira, down five kobo.
Ashaka Cement and Guinness were each two kobo down at 19.38 naira and 6.58 naira, respectively.
Guaranty Trust Bank shares dropped 10 kobo to 13.80 naira as more holders chose to take profit. NAL Merchant Bank also fell five kobo to 5.15 naira.
